reading_P_private_values.statement: x, W[j,:], y are the prover's private input; the verifier learns the roots (through O), h_O, h_L and the verdict. Leaf identities, ranks, layouts and counts are public in O.
code: packages/verity/src/verity/verification/wire.py:465 'The canonical bytes of a witness (the guest's private input)'; binding.py: public values = h_O || h_L || verdict (65 bytes), nothing else.

backends/gkr/PROTOCOL.md section 1: x_u (per-unit words, hints, row columns) public? **no**; section 7: only collision resistance of H is assumed for soundness, hiding beyond CRH is an extra assumption; backends/direct/PROTOCOL.md sections 1, 7, 8 likewise.

packages/verity/src/verity/verification/packed.py: 'the guest authenticates the whole packed leaf against the committed root, then reads the word at the statement-fixed index'; 'a leaf is hashed once however many positions read words of it'; canonical_id/dtype/shape are the prover's to supply.
reading_P_private_values.consequence: the ZK requirement is over the opened values (and the leaf digests, which are committed material); option (b) is excluded; (c) adds a hiding assumption on SHA-256 for disclosed leaf digests.

reading_C_values_in_clear.statement: the reference checkers (transparent.py, packed.check_packed_openings) see openings in the clear and say they are not ZK; nothing in verity.commitments forbids a verifier that sees values, but such a backend is NON_ZK_PROOF at best.
code: packages/verity/src/verity/verification/transparent.py:10: the reference checker is 'not zero-knowledge; it is the reference every other backend must agree with' -- it sees openings in the clear.

options.title: (a) SHA-256 Merkle openings inside the proof
options.hiding_assumption: none beyond the protocols' CRH: only roots (in O) and the verdict leave the proof
notes: whole leaf + node/lift chain in circuit; the first public-framing blocks of each leaf (5 compressions per instance before sharing) have a public chaining state and could be skipped (not credited here)

options.title: (b) openings checked by the verifier outside the proof (values public)
options.hiding_assumption: n/a: x, W, y are public to the verifier
notes: verifier sees x, W[j,:] and the whole output row in the clear: incompatible with reading P; NON_ZK_PROOF at best; the proof adds one linear 'committed word = public word' constraint per word (3073 per instance)

options.title: (c) recommitment: in-circuit SHA-256 of the leaf only, path outside
options.hiding_assumption: leaf digests disclosed: hiding of a 3072/4096-byte row under SHA-256 preimage resistance (beyond CRH)
notes: leaf digests disclosed to the verifier (hiding of the row under SHA-256 preimage resistance: an assumption beyond CRH, PROTOCOL.md section 7 of both candidates); the verifier folds the Merkle paths natively

options.title: (d) protocol change: Poseidon2-Goldilocks leaves, all inside
options.hiding_assumption: none beyond CRH of Poseidon2 (a new assumption set: Poseidon2 replaces SHA-256 as the protocol hash)
notes: changes verity.commitments (verity-vllm/leaf/v1 -> a Poseidon2 leaf scheme) and every recorded root, conformance vector and the SP1 guest: a protocol decision (README 'Commitments'), not a backend optimisation

killing_question.question: does authentication dominate again for either candidate under the options compatible with the privacy model?
killing_question.answer: yes for every SHA-256 option compatible with reading P ((a) and (c)): at B=4096 authentication is a multiple of the whole relation-only census for both candidates in every sharing regime; only the protocol change (d) brings it to the same order as the relation (A: gates ~ 1x, no extra committed elements but ~5 700 chained layers; B: committed +~60%).
killing_question.why_sp1_differed: SP1 pays ~562 guest cycles per SHA-256 compression natively and ~10 M cycles for statement machinery + a relation that a zkVM executes as ordinary instructions; a purpose-built circuit makes the relation ~1000x cheaper while SHA-256 stays at ~26k gates per compression, so the ratio inverts.
killing_question.overnight_sweep_should_assume: relation-only numbers stay labelled authentication=excluded; add a separate authentication line costed as (c) with SHA-256 (the compatible baseline; W-row leaf dominates, 50 compressions per distinct row) and (d) as the protocol proposal; (b) only for NON_ZK diagnostics. Neither (a) nor (c) is affordable at B=4096 without weight-row leaf amortisation across proofs.

Candidate A's committed elements for SHA-256 are the bit decompositions of every 32-bit addition output plus the message bits (10 496 per compression, est.)
the bench dataset's 24 seeds are 24 (x, output-row) pairs with all W rows distinct ('bench24'); 'none' and 'one_row' bracket it
field-operation fractions scale the accountants' relation-side rates (F_t mult-eq. per mul gate for A, per committed element for B); estimates
Poseidon2 packs 3 BF16 words per Goldilocks element; a 2-to-1 node is one permutation; no range openings (leaves.py: not carried yet)
